tasks.short: Warn maintenance workers and direct evacuation from radiation hazards

steps.what: Assess radiation hazard indications and identify exposed workers
Warn maintenance workers of the identified radiation hazards
outputs: hazard warning delivered to maintenance workers

steps.what: Direct workers to vacate hazardous areas
Confirm workers received directions and respond to difficulties
outputs: confirmed understanding and assessed evacuation difficulties

tasks.design: Retain the technician's immediate hazard assessment and direct communication through existing {TELEPHONY} and site procedures. Existing {OPS_SYSTEM} indications inform the technician; no new automatic warning, control or evacuation decision is proposed.
tasks.previous_blocker: The task depends on current physical conditions and whether workers understand the warning.
tasks.enabler_now: No supported digital substitution removes the technician's communication or situational assessment time in this task.
tasks.still_hard: Worker locations, changing conditions and failed communication require immediate human response.
tasks.human_edge: Recognise danger and make sure actual people receive and understand directions.
tasks.altitude: Keep the safety communication responsibility explicit.

reach.learn: Confirm understanding and raise communication difficulties immediately.

evidence.claim: This immediate warning and evacuation communication remains a human task; there is no measured basis for a time reduction here.

assumptions: The boundary includes assessment, the warning, separate evacuation directions and confirmation. The statement does not establish a record-writing duty, so no trailing report is invented.

Existing site instruments produce current indications, and the technician identifies workers and interprets conditions in s1; all observation time is retained. Missing or ambiguous indications require existing human safety procedures, not inferred structured hazard flags.
Native alarms and radio settings may support current work, but their existing runtime does not remove a priced human step here.
Communication gates are the technician's immediate check of the actual warning or direction and its recipients, not a new approval meeting. Maintenance workers are internal colleagues.
unknowns: The site's existing alarm coverage and communication arrangements.
research_questions: Observe existing drills to identify communication gaps without assuming that warning time can be removed.

already_counted.description: Assess hazards and confirm workers' understanding

incremental.description: No new system or maintenance work is introduced

approvals.approved_version: Actual hazard warning, affected area and worker recipients, checked against current conditions before delivery; changed conditions require a fresh warning check.
Actual evacuation direction, affected workers and current area information; check any changed direction immediately before delivery.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: E1: B=100, R=100, no incremental upkeep. All assessment and immediate communication remain; no current lookup, template entry or record write has been demonstrated as removable. Both range cases therefore retain the full task.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Coordinate accelerator support-system readiness with maintenance personnel

steps.what: Review accelerator support-system status and current maintenance information
Communicate with maintenance personnel about support-system readiness
Resolve unclear readiness information and agree outstanding maintenance actions
outputs: understood readiness state and outstanding actions

tasks.design: Configure a native {OPS_SYSTEM} view that brings existing support-system displays and maintenance references together. The technician still discusses readiness with maintenance personnel and resolves uncertain information; the view does not certify readiness or operate the accelerator.
tasks.previous_blocker: Switching between existing status displays and maintenance references may lengthen preparation.
tasks.enabler_now: A native view can reduce navigation where current status sources are already available.
tasks.still_hard: A displayed status may not capture unresolved maintenance concerns or operational context.
tasks.human_edge: Ask the right questions and recognise when apparently ready equipment still needs investigation.
tasks.altitude: Improve access to status information while preserving maintenance coordination.

reach.learn: Distinguish observed state from unresolved work and assumptions.

evidence.claim: Native status views could remove limited screen navigation; they do not establish accelerator readiness or measured communication savings.

assumptions: The boundary includes the current information lookup and conversation. No additional readiness log is assumed merely to create an automation benefit.

Existing instrumentation produces status indications. Maintenance personnel produce dated equipment-specific updates in their current maintenance process; s1 includes retrieval and checking currency, and s2/s3 retain clarification time. Missing or stale updates require speaking with personnel, not treating a blank field as ready.
The proposed 3-hour reduction removes only repeated navigation within s1; it leaves 17 of 20 hours for reading and reconciliation. Native views are tried before integration.
No machine alert, automatic readiness flag or operation authorisation is added.
unknowns: Whether status displays and maintenance updates can share a native view.
Whether today's preparation already uses a single view.
research_questions: Time current navigation separately from reading and maintenance discussion for several readiness checks.

incremental.description: Maintain status-view links and equipment references

approvals.approved_version: Actual support-system information and maintenance recipients, checked for equipment identity and currency before communication; changes require a new check.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: E1: B=100, R=97, gross 3 minus 1 upkeep gives central net 2. Conservative case: incompatible or stale status references retain 19/20 lookup hours plus all 80 communication/resolution hours: 99 retained, 1 gross minus 1 =0. A compatible native view retains 18 lookup hours plus 80 other hours: 98 retained, 2 gross minus 1 =1. An existing single view supplies no eligible navigation saving.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Determine or recommend radioactive decontamination procedures

steps.what: Assess equipment size, nature and degree of contamination
Retrieve applicable radioactive decontamination procedures and equipment restrictions
Determine the appropriate procedure and case-specific restrictions
outputs: selected procedure with rationale and restrictions

steps.what: Write the decontamination recommendation for the responsible work team
inputs: selected procedure with rationale and restrictions

steps.what: Communicate the recommended procedure and restrictions to colleagues

tasks.design: Configure native {DOCS} procedure views and recommendation headings that retain controlled procedure references. The technician assesses contamination, chooses the procedure, writes the case-specific recommendation and checks the exact advice before communicating it.
tasks.previous_blocker: Finding the current applicable procedure and repeating document references can accompany the substantive recommendation.
tasks.enabler_now: Controlled document metadata and reusable headings may remove lookup and reference formatting effort.
tasks.still_hard: The equipment and contamination context determine whether a procedure is appropriate.
tasks.human_edge: Recognise the limits of standard procedures and the need for further specialist assessment.
tasks.altitude: Improve recommendation traceability while retaining technical judgement.

reach.learn: Keep measurements, equipment context and controlled references together.

evidence.claim: Controlled document views and reference headings could reduce limited retrieval and formatting; procedure choice remains human and the proposed savings are unmeasured.

assumptions: The scenario includes a written recommendation actually used by the responsible team; it does not append a new activity record. Oral-only advice has no eligible writing baseline.

The technician assesses equipment identity, size, material and condition and checks measurement time, location, value and unit in s1, with all that time retained. Existing qualified measurement personnel produce contamination results in the current measurement process. Missing provenance requires manual investigation before recommending a procedure.

Document control staff maintain procedure identifiers and versions. S2 retains applicability checking; a native view removes only 3 hours of navigation. The writing template removes only 2 hours of headings and repeated references, retaining the full case-specific rationale.
No automatic procedure selection, generated technical instruction or equipment control is proposed. Ordinary author saves remain retained without self-approval.
unknowns: Whether controlled metadata support a useful native document view.
Whether the current recommendation is written and how much reference formatting it contains.
research_questions: Compare current recommendation preparation with a native reference template, including difficult applicability cases.

already_counted.description: Assess the case and determine appropriate procedures

incremental.description: Maintain controlled procedure view and reference headings

approvals.approved_version: Exact recommendation, equipment scope, controlled procedure versions, restrictions and work-team recipients; changed advice requires a new check before communication.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: E1: B=100, R=95, gross 5 minus 1 upkeep gives central net 4. Conservative case: weak procedure metadata retain all 15 lookup hours and minimal reusable references retain 19/20 writing hours plus 65 other hours: 99 retained, 1 gross minus 1 =0. With usable controlled identifiers, retain 13 lookup and 19 writing hours plus 65 other hours: 97 retained, 3 gross minus 1 =2.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

role.altitude: Preserve direct safety communication and technical judgement while reducing demonstrated document navigation and formatting.
reach: Coordinate current information with maintenance and radiation protection colleagues.
role.ambitious_version: Technicians supported by current, traceable information without automatic safety decisions or unused records.
